I've recently lost a reasonable amount of weight through a calorie controlled diet, and am now looking to train myself to be stronger and generally fitter.

I'm a new member of a general fitness 24/7 gym, and they offer personal training but it's not something I can afford at the moment. What are the best resources for getting started in the gym? How do I begin measuring my progress? Is it worth getting a Xiaomi fitness band?

When I first started I watched a lot of Youtube videos of different exercises. I would go into the gym (after some at home research) with a short workout plan and my phone. If I got nervous about a move I wanted to try I would look it up and watch a video and then try it out in front of the mirrors with a lightweight or just the bar, trying to match what I saw in the video. If you are doing or wanting to do the big compound lifts don't be afraid to just use the bar or even an ez/straight bar to start until you have the movement and form down.

These days I like to use the Bodyspace App from Bodybulding.com. Its a great resource for making or finding and tracking workouts. An added bonus is that for every exercise in their database they have an exercise guide with a written description and most have a video. It shows previous workouts and 1RMs to help measure your progress.

Hope this helps a little bit.
